hypotheses.text: Across the foundational cohort delineated by Kaiyrzhanov et al. (2022) and indexed under OMIM #620938, the true denominator of individuals presenting with the spastic paraplegia spectrum is 16 of 19 (84.2%), while 3 of 19 (15.8%) present with severe infantile hypotonia/encephalopathy without spasticity.
hypotheses.rationale: Clarifying the exact denominator is critical because OMIM #620938 and prior literature have cited differing subgroup sizes (13 versus 16 versus 19 patients). Establishing whether denominators are computed over all NFU1 missense patients (n=19) or restricted to those exhibiting spasticity and prolonged survival (n=16) directly determines the calculated diagnostic sensitivity of cerebellar signs, optic atrophy, and neuropathy.

evidence.text: Kaiyrzhanov et al. (2022) report 19 affected individuals from 10 families, where 16 of 19 exhibit prolonged survival with early-onset pure to complex hereditary spastic paraplegia phenotypes, whereas 3 of 19 display severe hypotonia and neurodevelopmental delay.

hypotheses.text: Cerebellar signs (cerebellar ataxia and dysarthria) are present in the majority of surviving SPG93 patients, with a prevalence between 60% and 75% (approximately 10/16 to 12/16), establishing that SPG93 manifests predominantly as a complex hereditary spastic paraplegia rather than pure spastic paraplegia.
hypotheses.rationale: Differentiating pure from complex HSP is the first branch point in adult/pediatric spasticity diagnosis. If cerebellar signs affect over 60% of individuals, pure spastic paraplegia represents an early or minor presentation, and finding cerebellar signs should significantly elevate clinical suspicion for SPG93.

evidence.text: The provided snippet states that NFU1 missense variants produce a phenotypic spectrum ranging from early-onset pure to complex hereditary spastic paraplegia, but exact individual counts for cerebellar ataxia are not detailed in the abstract snippet alone.

hypotheses.text: Optic atrophy is an uncommon manifestation in SPG93, present in fewer than 20% (≤3/16) of assessed patients, providing a discriminator against mitochondrial complex spastic paraplegias (e.g., SPG7, ACO2, or OPA1-related disease) where optic atrophy occurs in >50% of cases.
hypotheses.rationale: Mitochondrial leukodystrophies and complex HSPs frequently involve the optic nerve. A low frequency of optic atrophy in SPG93 would mean that prominent optic atrophy should point clinicians toward alternative complex HSP or primary mitochondrial gene diagnoses.

evidence.text: In literature reviewing NFU1-related disease and MMDS1, optic atrophy is not listed among the defining core cardinal criteria (which focus on leukoencephalopathy, lactic acidosis, pulmonary hypertension, or spastic paraplegia), suggesting it is not a hallmark finding in NFU1 spectrum disorders.

hypotheses.text: Peripheral polyneuropathy in SPG93 exhibits age-dependent penetrance, being present on electrophysiological assessment in at least 50% (≥8/16) of individuals over 10 years of age, but absent in patients under 5 years of age who frequently present with isolated spastic diplegia.
hypotheses.rationale: Distal axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy often takes years to develop in inborn errors of metabolism affecting the pyramidal tracts. If neuropathy is consistently absent under age 5, clinicians should not rule out SPG93 in toddlers presenting with spastic diplegia mimicking cerebral palsy.

evidence.text: Mahmoud et al. (2025) describe a young child with NFU1-related disease who initially presented with milder pure spastic diplegia that was misdiagnosed as cerebral palsy and managed with an intrathecal baclofen pump, corroborating that younger patients exhibit isolated spasticity prior to the emergence of complex multi-system signs.

new_directions.question_text: What are the exact patient-by-patient clinical counts and HPO term annotations in Table 1 and the supplementary clinical data of Kaiyrzhanov et al. (2022) for cerebellar ataxia, dysarthria, optic atrophy, and peripheral neuropathy across all 19 patients?
new_directions.rationale: Extracting the complete clinical matrix from the full text of Kaiyrzhanov et al. (2022) is required to replace estimated ranges with exact numerators and denominators for statistical diagnostic weighting.

new_directions.question_text: In subsequent case reports outside the original Kaiyrzhanov cohort (such as Mahmoud et al. 2025 and Rudenskaya et al. 2025), what proportion of SPG93 patients exhibit peripheral polyneuropathy and optic atrophy upon electrophysiological and ophthalmological follow-up?
new_directions.rationale: Validating the prevalence of complex features in independent, post-2022 case descriptions tests whether the original cohort suffered from ascertainment bias toward complex phenotypes.
